claims.text: A neural-network interatomic potential trained on diverse ab initio configurations of multicomponent HEAs can serve as a superior thermodynamic-integration reference compared with traditional EAM potentials.
A neural-network potential captures the many-body and local-environment effects of the liquid state more accurately than an EAM potential.
The proposed system is a multicomponent HEA, such as CrMnFeNi, in crystalline and liquid phases near its melting temperature.
The proposed intervention is to train a neural-network potential on ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations that sample the liquid's configurational diversity.
The trained neural-network potential will be used as the reference Hamiltonian in thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method is applicable to HEAs containing four or more components over approximately 0.9–1.1 T_m.
Liquid disorder is significant over approximately 0.9–1.1 T_m.
Representing many-body interactions and variations in local coordination improves phase-space overlap between neural-network-reference and ab initio liquid configurations.
The neural-network potential captures a broader and more accurate spectrum of liquid configurations than the more rigid EAM functional form.
More accurate representation of liquid configurations minimizes discrepancies in sampling the ab initio liquid free-energy landscape.
A closer match to the ab initio energy surface reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The neural-network reference could reduce integration errors by approximately an order of magnitude relative to TOR-TILD using EAM references.
TOR-TILD currently employs EAM potentials as thermodynamic-integration references.
The limited flexibility of EAM potentials prevents them from fully representing the configurational diversity of ab initio liquids in multicomponent HEAs.
The EAM representation limitation causes significant phase-space-overlap problems and thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The intervention is expected to work for chemically disordered multicomponent systems near melting.
Performance may be limited in alloys with strongly directional covalent or ionic bonding.
Performance may be limited when local environments lie outside those represented by the training data.
The hypothesis will be tested by comparing EAM-reference and neural-network-reference thermodynamic integration against an independent ab initio free-energy calculation.

The hypothesis is falsified if the neural-network reference fails to reduce path mismatch by at least 50% with statistical significance and has phase-space sampling quality comparable to the EAM reference across independent runs.
